findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the wording: state that the loop STRUCTURE is unchanged but each entry now dispatches through hash_dep_entry (plain path → _hash_file, glob pattern → membership digest) on BOTH the signing and re-check sides.
evidence: "compute_validity's per-path re-hash loop is unchanged — it still iterates the concrete recorded entries"
"Signing (dependency_hashes) and the claim-gate re-check (compute_validity, _rehash) both call it, so the two sides cannot diverge"
findings.finding: Section (b) states 'compute_validity's per-path re-hash loop is unchanged' yet later says compute_validity/_rehash both call the new hash_dep_entry helper (dispatching glob patterns to a membership digest). The re-hash step is in fact changed — it must now dispatch per entry rather than call _hash_file directly.
findings.location: Section (b), 'compute_validity's per-path re-hash loop is unchanged' vs 'Signing ... and the claim-gate re-check (compute_validity, _rehash) both call it'
scenarios: An implementer reads 'unchanged' and leaves _rehash calling _hash_file, breaking glob-pattern membership-digest entries at claim-gate time.
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'the re-hash loop is unchanged' to 'the re-hash loop's iteration is unchanged, but each entry is now hashed via hash_dep_entry, which dispatches glob patterns to the membership digest'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the (b) claim that `compute_validity`'s re-hash loop 'is unchanged' with routing through `hash_dep_entry`: name the inline `_hash_file` call at attest.py:568-576 as an edit target (it is a distinct site from `_rehash`) so glob PATTERN dep entries re-hash via the membership-digest branch at claim time.
evidence: attest.py:568-576 (DEFAULT profile): `deps = manifest_deps(auth_manifest)` then `drifted = [p for p, digest in sorted(deps.items()) if _hash_file(p, base=base) != digest]` — an inline _hash_file call, NOT a call to _rehash

attest.py:204-208: `_rehash` is a SEPARATE function; its only callers are drift_refresh_candidate (attest.py:241) and refresh_attestation (attest.py:288), NOT the compute_validity DEFAULT claim-gate path

Plan (b): 'compute_validity's per-path re-hash loop is unchanged — it still iterates the concrete recorded entries' vs 'Signing (dependency_hashes) and the claim-gate re-check (compute_validity, _rehash) both call it'
findings.finding: The plan names `hash_dep_entry` callers as `dependency_hashes` and `compute_validity`/`_rehash`, but `compute_validity`'s DEFAULT claim-gate re-hash loop calls `_hash_file` INLINE (attest.py:575), not `_rehash` — yet the plan also states that loop 'is unchanged'. These two claims contradict: for a glob PATTERN dep entry (membership digest) to re-verify, the inline `_hash_file(p, base=base)` at attest.py:575 must itself dispatch through `hash_dep_entry`, otherwise the pattern is hashed as a literal filename to `_ABSENT_HASH` and mismatches the signed membership digest on every claim, invalidating unconditionally.
findings.location: Section (b), 'Both sides route through ONE helper …' and 'compute_validity's per-path re-hash loop is unchanged'
scenarios: A no-file-impact ticket whose signed dep set includes a glob PATTERN entry (e.g. `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/*.md`) with a membership digest; at claim time compute_validity's DEFAULT loop hashes the pattern string as a filename, gets _ABSENT_HASH, and reports stale-code even when the membership is unchanged.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the claim-gate DEFAULT loop in compute_validity (attest.py:568-576) is changed to call `read_set.hash_dep_entry(p, base=base)` instead of `_hash_file(p, base=base)`, and that `_rehash` (attest.py:204) is likewise routed through it so the drift_refresh/refresh_attestation paths agree; drop the 'is unchanged' wording.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the hash_dep_entry routing inventory with attest.py:575: state explicitly that compute_validity's DEFAULT drift loop switches from `_hash_file(p, base=base)` to `hash_dep_entry(p, base=base)` (it does not go through `_rehash`), and drop the 'per-path re-hash loop is unchanged' wording that contradicts it.
evidence: Plan: 'Signing (dependency_hashes) and the claim-gate re-check (compute_validity, _rehash) both call it, so the two sides cannot diverge.'
Plan: "compute_validity's per-path re-hash loop is unchanged — it still iterates the concrete recorded entries."

attest.py:573-575 — the claim-gate DEFAULT drift loop calls `_hash_file(p, base=base)` directly (NOT `_rehash`): `drifted = [p for p, digest in sorted(deps.items()) if _hash_file(p, base=base) != digest]`.
manifest.py:184-185 — `_hash_file` returns `_ABSENT_HASH` for any path it cannot open, so a glob-pattern membership-digest entry (e.g. `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/*.md`) never matches its signed digest.
findings.finding: The patch-site inventory for routing hashing through the new hash_dep_entry helper omits (and contradicts itself on) compute_validity's DEFAULT-profile drift loop at attest.py:575. That loop calls _hash_file(p, base=base) directly, not _rehash; the plan names compute_validity as a hash_dep_entry caller yet also declares its per-path loop 'unchanged.' Since _hash_file returns _ABSENT_HASH for any non-openable path (manifest.py:184-185), a recorded glob-PATTERN membership-digest line handled by the unchanged loop mismatches the signed digest on every check.
findings.location: Section (b), 'Both sides route through ONE helper … Signing (dependency_hashes) and the claim-gate re-check (compute_validity, _rehash) both call it' vs. 'compute_validity's per-path re-hash loop is unchanged — it still iterates the concrete recorded entries.'
scenarios: attest.py:575 inline loop: left calling _hash_file (as 'unchanged' says), a recorded membership-digest line like `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/*.md` hashes to _ABSENT_HASH and never equals the signed digest → every no-file-impact ticket with blast-radius globs is perpetually invalidated, the exact over-invalidation the plan removes.

_rehash (attest.py:208) feeds drift_refresh_candidate (attest.py:241), refresh_attestation (attest.py:288) and orchestrator.py:570 — if the plan converts _rehash but leaves the compute_validity inline loop, the drift-refresh reuse path and the primary claim gate disagree on glob entries.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the `_hash_file(p, base=base)` call in the compute_validity DEFAULT drift loop (attest.py:575) with `hash_dep_entry(p, base=base)`, and enumerate all _hash_file re-hash sites converted (attest.py:575, _rehash at attest.py:208) so the loop dispatching on glob metacharacters matches signing.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the two criteria_routing.json paths in the blast-radius list against the existing regver stamp: either exclude them (already covered by registry_version) or state why a hard stale-code invalidation should co-exist with the grandfathered registry_drift, so the routing-edit outcome is unambiguous.
evidence: registry_version already hashes EFFECTIVE routing: 'the stamp hashes the repo's EFFECTIVE routing (packaged ⊕ the .rebar/criteria_routing.json overlay) plus the overlay's activated-project ids' (manifest.py:132-135)
Both routing JSONs appear in the plan's blast-radius list: '.rebar/criteria_routing.json ... src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json'

regver drift is grandfathered/non-blocking: 'a rotated stamp is GRANDFATHERED at the claim gate: it is reported as non-blocking registry_drift rather than invalidating' (manifest.py:134-137), whereas a dep-hash mismatch returns verdict 'stale-code' (attest.py:577-584)

criteria/**, reviewers/*.md, and gates/*.yaml are NOT covered by regver (its basis is the routing index + CANONICAL_DET/LLM/GROUNDED id sets, manifest.py:160-165), so only the two routing JSONs are redundant
findings.finding: The blast-radius glob list hardcodes `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`, but both files are already bound into the same signed manifest via the existing `regver:` stamp (registry_version hashes the EFFECTIVE routing = packaged routing + the overlay). This is an overlapping/duplicate invalidation surface for the same two files, and the two mechanisms disagree on outcome: a routing edit invalidates as grandfathered non-blocking `registry_drift` (ADR 0053) via regver, but as hard `stale-code` via the new dep entry. The plan does not reconcile the overlap or the conflicting severity.
findings.location: Section (b), 'Blast-radius entries' list; cross-ref manifest.py:125-171 (registry_version) and manifest.py:437 (dep lines)
scenarios: A reviewer edits `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` after a no-file-impact attestation: regver rotates (grandfathered, non-blocking) AND the dep/membership-digest leg fires (hard stale-code) — two mechanisms, opposite blocking outcomes, for one file.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` from the blast-radius list (both are already bound via regver) and keep only the entries regver does not cover: criteria/**, reviewers/*.md, gates/*.yaml, plus rebar.toml. Add a one-line note that routing JSONs are covered by the regver stamp, not the dep set.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how hash_dep_entry distinguishes a curated blast-radius GLOB PATTERN from a read-set/cited PLAIN PATH that merely contains a glob metacharacter (e.g. only treat the known blast-radius pattern set as globs, or add an existence-precheck so an existing regular file always hash_files regardless of metacharacters), so a literally-named file is not misrouted to a membership digest.
evidence: The dispatch key is purely syntactic: 'glob → membership digest, plain path → the existing _hash_file'

read-set entries originate from fetch_target's read_file path arg (usage_log.py:282-310) and _cited_paths (manifest.py:188) — arbitrary agent-supplied paths, not a curated pattern list, unlike the blast-radius globs
Normalization step 4 (os.path.relpath + PurePath.as_posix()) collapses ./ and .. but does NOT strip *, ?, or [ from a literal filename
For blast-radius patterns the glob interpretation is intended; for read-set/cited entries it is not — the same syntactic test governs both classes
findings.finding: hash_dep_entry dispatches glob-vs-plain-path on the presence of a glob metacharacter (*, ?, [), but read-set and cited paths are arbitrary agent read_file targets, not curated patterns. A regular file whose real path contains one of those characters (legal on POSIX) would be misclassified as a glob and get a membership digest instead of its file-content hash — the wrong currency semantics on BOTH the signing and re-check sides.
findings.location: Section (b), 'Both sides route through ONE helper, read_set.hash_dep_entry(entry, base=...), dispatching on a glob metacharacter (*, ?, [)'
scenarios: A review reads or cites a regular file whose path contains a literal bracket/glob character (e.g. a test fixture 'cases[edge].json'); at sign time it becomes a membership digest over a match list rather than a content hash, and content edits to that exact file no longer invalidate as intended
findings.suggested_fix: Classify by ORIGIN, not syntax: apply the glob branch only to the fixed blast-radius pattern list, and always route read-set/cited entries through _hash_file (they already passed the step-5 existing-regular-file filter). Alternatively, in hash_dep_entry try _hash_file first for any path that resolves to an existing regular file and only fall back to membership-digest for the curated patterns.
